To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) pleasant and unpleasant pictures, but not neutral pictures, elicited an early endogenous negativity over temporo-occiptal sensor sites; (b) pleasant and unpleasant images elicited enlarged late-positive potentials over central-parietal sensor locations relative to neutral pictures; (c) pleasant and unpleasant stimuli elicited enlarged late-negative potentials over fronto-central sensor sites relative to the neutral stimuli; (d) the late-negative potentials were more pronounced in response to unpleasant than pleasant images
The selective processing of brief affective pictures was investigated using dense sensor arrays.
